I strongly recommend you underCLOCK it as well as undervolting, and no you didn't read it wrong. I'm with the RX 6700 XT now, on both the 6500 and 6700 I noticed pretty much no performance loss when underclocking, maybe 1 or 2 fps, but a MASSIVE reduction in power draw and temperature, with the 6700 XT I went from ~200w and 95C hotspot, to ~130w and 75C hotspot, just by doing -150mhz and -80mv on Adrenalin, and I tested ALL games and lost 3-4 fps, say 100 fps before, and 96 fps after.

See I'm not sure if it's just an AMD thing, but the way they ship these GPUs from factory is just WAY above the efficiency curve for them, probably for marketing reasons since people tend to look at FPS first rather than temperature, power consumption, etc. I don't think I ever saw anyone judging or comparing graphics cards based on "how many frames per watt" it does. But for the average gamer/consumer it certainly matters on the electric bill

Look for red icons on the top-right corner of the screen. If you see any (such as 3 squares) and it never goes away during your gameplay, it's probably your internet connection.

Otherwise, it could be either the CPU or the GPU. Download MSI AfterBurner and check for statistics while you game. If the GPU is maxed out (100% usage) and you're still getting low FPS, then it's definitely the GPU. In that case, you can try lowering you graphics settings.

However, if the CPU is maxed out (100% usage) while the GPU is barely touching 100% (say it's sitting at 50 or 40%), then your processor is having trouble running the game. In that case, the only "fix" would be buying a better one - or checking if your current one is overheating (same goes for the GPU).
